accepted.sentence: In frost-free tropical and subtropical regions, growers cultivate this crop outdoors because prolonged cold can injure its leaves and roots.
Acidic, sandy soils suit its cultivation, while poorly drained ground can encourage root diseases.
Fields exposed to heavy rainfall may use raised beds to let excess water drain away from the roots.
Commercial growers often cover planting beds with dark plastic mulch to suppress weeds and conserve moisture around young plants.
In cooler climates, gardeners may keep it in a sunny container and move it indoors before temperatures approach freezing.
Where dry seasons interrupt rainfall, supplemental irrigation can support steady growth and dependable fruit development.
On tropical farms, it is generally planted in open, sunny plots rather than dense shade, which can limit its growth.
Because crops take months to mature, farms may stagger planting dates to spread harvesting across the year.
